why: note-flush should touch this file about once a minute; a stale heartbeat means the outbox is not draining and peer notes are stuck
fix: check that the note-flush timer (cron/launchd/systemd --user) is installed and running on this machine, per the multi skill's install docs; on Windows it is the Task Scheduler task 'note-flush' (Get-ScheduledTask note-flush)

why: the master kill switch that silences every working-smarter feature (goal card, janitor) at once
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check: remove the file to turn features back on, create it to silence them

why: the total kill switch for the PreToolUse agent-dispatch-guard hook
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check: remove the file to re-enable the guard, create it to silence it

why: flips the dispatch guard from advisory to enforced (advisory mode evaluates and logs silently and never prints anything to the agent; only enforced mode can deny or add context)
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check: create the file to enforce the guard, remove it to keep it advisory

why: widens which peer-note kinds are allowed to wake an idle pane
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check

why: disables the flusher's typed-into-composer delivery path
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check

why: the feature kill switch for hooks/backlog-notice.js (the master ws-off switch silences it too)
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check: remove the file to turn the backlog notice back on, create it to silence it

why: lean agents (builder, integrator, reviewer, runner) do not load the user's ~/.claude rules files; this file is where the user's personal hard stops reach them
fix: create ~/.agents/lean-rules.md (owned by the user, at most 40 lines) with the personal hard stops a lean agent should still obey - the plugin does not ship this file

why: this pane's peer-note inbox registers from its session name (/rename <slug> or claude --name <slug>) first, or NOTE_SLUG, or a panes.json binding - this check only sees NOTE_SLUG, so a pane named the new way may correctly show 'not set' here while still being fully registered
fix: no fix needed either way, this is a visibility check: name the session with /rename <slug> (the primary route, docs/pane-setup.md), or fall back to NOTE_SLUG=<slug> in the --command string, or bind by hand with `note-inbox --bind <slug>`

why: the plugin's own hooks/hooks.json still registers the PreToolUse delete-guard hook under the Bash|PowerShell matcher; if it is not wired, nothing in this plugin catches an accidental rm -rf
fix: reinstall or repair the plugin so Claude Code re-registers the PreToolUse delete-guard hook from the plugin's own hooks/hooks.json

why: the plugin's own hooks/hooks.json still registers the PostToolUse multi-inbox hook, which delivers a peer note into this session after a tool call; without it a sent note never reaches the pane
fix: reinstall or repair the plugin so Claude Code re-registers the PostToolUse multi-inbox hook from the plugin's own hooks/hooks.json

why: the PreToolUse delete-guard hook registration is useless if the script it runs is missing
fix: reinstall or repair the plugin so hooks/delete-guard.mjs is present at its install root

why: the PostToolUse multi-inbox hook registration is useless if the script it runs is missing
fix: reinstall or repair the plugin so hooks/multi-inbox.js is present at its install root

why: the note-send shim on PATH is how a peer note is actually sent from a shell; without it a caller has to know the longer node invocation, or sending silently fails
fix: run node scripts/mirror-shared-skills.mjs to (re)generate the PATH shims into ~/.local/bin

why: peer notes and the flusher's own state live under ~/.agents/notes; if the directory itself is missing, nothing on this host has ever run that creates it
fix: run any note-flush/note-send/note-inbox command once, or create it by hand: mkdir -p ~/.agents/notes

why: without "crossSessionInbound": "accept" in Claude's own settings, an arriving peer note is held behind a modal approval dialog instead of delivered, and the sender cannot tell

the daily janitor timer's own log proves it actually ran in the last 26 hours; a log still absent more than 26 hours after install means the schedule stopped firing. An absent log right after install is expected — the timer has no earlier trigger to catch up on, so it stays missing until the first scheduled run (up to ~24h later)
fix: check the host's own scheduler first (systemd --user list-timers janitor-record.timer, the Windows task janitor-record, or the launchd agent) to confirm it is registered and enabled; only rerun scripts/install-janitor-timer.mjs with --enable if the timer is not registered there
